reviewed_by: Gemini Pro blind reviewer, batch G2-NA-Q4-Harden (mat_g2_na_q4_5), 2026-08-18

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The samples directly fulfill the MATATAG competency 'Order similar fractions from smallest to largest, and vice versa.' The item set provides both ascending tasks such as "Which list shows these fractions ordered from smallest to largest: 2/4, 3/4, 1/4?" (seed 42) and descending tasks such as "Order these fractions from largest to smallest: 1/4, 2/4, 3/4." (seed 43) and "Arrange these fractions from greatest to least: 2/8, 3/8, 7/8, 6/8." (seed 50). In all cases, students must compare and sequence sets of fractions with common denominators.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Coverage is thorough across both ordering directions (smallest to largest vs. largest to smallest / greatest to least), list lengths (3 and 4 fractions), and standard Grade 2 denominators (/4, /5, /6, /8). Examples include 3-item fourths in "Order these fractions from smallest to largest: 3/4, 2/4, 1/4." (seed 46), 4-item eighths in "Order these fractions from largest to smallest: 1/8, 5/8, 2/8, 7/8." (seed 44), 4-item sixths in "Order these fractions from largest to smallest: 5/6, 1/6, 4/6, 2/6." (seed 45), and 4-item fifths in "Arrange these fractions from greatest to least: 2/5, 4/5, 3/5, 1/5." (seed 601).

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The cognitive demand is well-calibrated for Grade 2 Quarter 4 learners. Prompts are concise and use accessible language such as "Order these fractions from largest to smallest: 1/6, 3/6, 4/6, 2/6." (seed 502) and "Arrange these fractions from greatest to least: 4/8, 3/8, 5/8, 7/8." (seed 500). The fraction values are strictly proper fractions with identical denominators, allowing students to focus purely on numerator sequencing without requiring reduction, cross-multiplication, or common denominator computation.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The generator demonstrates diverse syntactic formulations and interaction formats. It incorporates direct imperative prompts like "Order these fractions from largest to smallest: 3/6, 1/6, 4/6, 5/6." (seed 600) and "Arrange these fractions from greatest to least: 2/8, 3/8, 7/8, 6/8." (seed 50), as well as question-based identification prompts like "Which list shows these fractions ordered from largest to smallest: 4/6, 2/6, 3/6, 5/6?" (seed 501) and "Which list shows these fractions ordered from smallest to largest: 2/4, 3/4, 1/4?" (seed 42), spanning both mcq and cloze formats.

competency_alignment.rationale: All items strictly adhere to the targeted competency. Every item presents a collection of similar proper fractions (e.g. "Order these fractions from largest to smallest: 5/6, 1/6, 4/6, 2/6." in seed 45) and evaluates ordering skill. There are no out-of-scope concepts such as unlike denominators, mixed numbers, improper fractions, or arithmetic operations.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The numerical magnitudes and set sizes are perfectly tailored for Grade 2. The denominators (4, 5, 6, 8) and list lengths (3 or 4 elements) are age-appropriate. Examples such as "Which list shows these fractions ordered from largest to smallest: 5/8, 2/8, 3/8, 6/8?" (seed 602) and "Arrange these fractions from greatest to least: 2/5, 4/5, 3/5, 1/5." (seed 601) stay within accessible limits while testing mastery of the ordering concept.
